derived_from.operation: image-generation edit to reduce surface variation and restate a compact repeated-material vocabulary while retaining the fortress composition

purpose: Test whether explicitly repeated masonry, rail, cloud, mountain and wood modules lower exact tile cost without losing the stage's key silhouettes.
exact_prompt: Reauthor this as a much simpler, genuinely tile-economical Mega Drive fighting-stage background concept, keeping the same Japanese night fortress identity and the same broad horizontal composition: compact keep to the right of center, small watchtower near far left, large pale moon in upper-right sky, broad mountain silhouette, continuous wooden fighting deck, regularly spaced guardrail posts, restrained lanterns. Make the art read clearly at 320x224 after nearest-neighbor reduction. Treat every material as a tiny repeatable 8x8 tile vocabulary: use only 2 repeated masonry motifs for all stone walls, 2 repeated wood-board motifs for the deck, 1 repeated rail-post motif, 2 broad cloud motifs, 2 mountain silhouette motifs, 1 dark water motif. Preserve the keep's outer silhouette and roof tiers as the only detailed unique architectural feature; express its walls with those same two repeated masonry motifs. Replace stone micro-bricks, wood grain scratches, tiny random lights, tiny highlights and varied per-post detail with broad hard-edged pixel clusters. Use a consistent 12-color maximum palette with a strong cool navy/blue night ramp, muted stone lavender/blue, warm dark wood and only a few bright amber lantern pixels plus pale moonlight; no dithering. Keep strong value separation behind two large fighters, a quiet clear floor and feet-contact line near the lower gameplay band. No HUD, fighters, text, logos, gradients, blur, glow, photorealism, scanlines, extra ornaments, or added objects. Preserve the source's established object placement and visual identity while deliberately removing texture variation; this is a production-art concept to be translated and measured, not finished native game art.
